issues.symptom: OpenBillow says the GPU engine (Warp) is not installed
issues.cause: The GPU engine is a separate 105 MB download. It needs Blender's online access to be on the first time.
fix: Open Preferences > System > Network and turn on Allow Online Access.
Open the OpenBillow add-on preferences and press Install GPU Engine.

issues.symptom: OpenBillow does not find a usable GPU
issues.cause: This version needs an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA (RTX 2000 series or newer). AMD, Intel and Apple GPUs are not supported.
fix: Run OpenBillow on a computer with a supported NVIDIA GPU.
On other hardware, use Blender's built-in Mantaflow simulation.

issues.symptom: A bake fails to start with an error about the NVIDIA driver or CUDA version
issues.cause: The installed NVIDIA driver is too old for the GPU engine, which needs a driver that supports CUDA 12 or newer.
fix: Install the current driver for your GPU from nvidia.com.

issues.symptom: The GPU engine download, presets or Send support request are unavailable
issues.cause: Blender's Allow Online Access setting is off, so the add-on will not use the network.
fix: Open Preferences > System > Network and turn on Allow Online Access.
If you need to keep it off, save the diagnostics to a file from the add-on preferences.

issues.symptom: A bake stops because the cache folder cannot be written
issues.cause: The domain's Cache folder does not exist, is read-only, or is on a drive that is full.
fix: Save the .blend file if the Cache folder is a relative path.
In the domain settings, set Cache to a folder you can write to, on a drive with free space.

issues.symptom: OpenBillow warns that the simulation will not fit in GPU memory
issues.cause: The memory estimate for this domain is larger than the memory on the GPU.
fix: Lower Resolution Divisions on the domain.
Turn off High Resolution if it is on.

issues.symptom: A bake stops with an out of memory error
issues.cause: The simulation needed more GPU memory than was free.
fix: Close other programs that use the GPU: games, browsers with hardware acceleration, other Blender windows.
Lower Resolution Divisions on the domain, or turn off High Resolution.
Set VRAM Limit (MB) in the add-on preferences so that a bake too large for your GPU is refused before it starts.

issues.symptom: A bake fails with an nvrtc or kernel compile error
issues.cause: The saved GPU kernels are often stale or damaged after an update of the GPU engine or the driver.
fix: Close Blender and delete the Warp kernel cache folder. It is rebuilt on the next bake.
On Linux it is ~/.cache/warp. On Windows it is %LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\warp\Cache.

issues.symptom: The first bake takes a long time to start
issues.cause: The first bake compiles the GPU kernels, which can take from tens of seconds to a few minutes. Later bakes reuse them.
fix: Wait for the first bake to finish compiling. No action is needed.
